summary: Kennard Lipman works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He completed his doctoral studies under Herbert V. Guenther and held a post as a sessional instructor at the University of Calgary.
Kenneth Doo Young Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Ryuichi Abe and held a post at Stetson University (attested 2007).

Kenneth G. Zysk specializes in Indology and religious studies. He earned an M.A. at UC Santa Barbara and a Ph.D. at Australian National University, holding posts at Eastern Michigan University, University of Copenhagen, UCLA, UW-Madison, and University of Toronto.

Kenneth J. Guest specializes in religious studies and Sinology. He studied at Columbia, Peking University, Union Theological Seminary, and CUNY, also studying under Aloysius Pieris. He has held teaching posts at Hunter College and Baruch College.

Kenneth J. Saunders (1883–1937) was a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Wagiswara. He served as Professor of the History of Religion at the Pacific School of Religion (~1921–1935) and lectured at the University of California.

Kenneth K. Inada (1923–2011) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He was a professor at the University at Buffalo (attested 1983–1999) and served as Chair of the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research from 1996 to 1999.

Kenneth K. Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and UC Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini. He held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1984–1998) and Musashino University (~1998–2018).

Kenneth Roy Norman (1925–2020) was an Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taunton School and Downing College. He held posts at the University of Cambridge (attested 1987–2001) and served as President of the Pali Text Society (1988).

Kenryo Minowa is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1981–1989). He held posts at Rissho University, the Eastern Institute, Aichi Gakuin University, Toyo University, and became a professor at the University of Tokyo in 2010.
Kenryu Nishio is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his doctorate at Otani University and served at Hanazono University, where he is attested as professor emeritus in 2014.
Kenryu Tsuji (1919–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his studies at Ryukoku University in 1938 and also studied at the University of Toronto.

Kenryu Tsukinowa (1888–1969) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Bukkyo University. He taught at Ryukoku University (~1928–1958), Bukkyo, Koyasan, and Shuchiin Universities, and founded the Tantric Buddhism Research Society in 1960.
Kenshi Kusano is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Otani University from ~1971 to 1979 and became a professor there around 1999.
Kensuke Nedachi specializes in history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University from ~1976 to 1984 and served as a professor there from ~2007 to 2021.

Kenta Suzuki is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Kyoto University (~1994–1998) and the University of Tokyo (~1998–2008), later serving as an associate professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College from around 2012.

Kenyu Mitomo is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Rissho University and UC Berkeley. He held long-term professorships and administrative roles at Rissho University (~1976–2015), along with appointments at Otani University and Chung-Hwa Institute.

Kevin A. Vose is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned degrees from Bates College and the University of Virginia, studying under doctoral supervisor Jeffrey Hopkins and traditional teacher Ngawang Jinpa.
Kevin Buckelew specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Sarah Lawrence College and pursued doctoral work under Chun-fang Yu, Bernard Faure, and Zhaohua Yang.

Khakyab Dorje (1871–1922) was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo (~1884–1892) and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thayé (~1886–1899), and later taught Kalu Rinpoche.

Khammai Dhammasami is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his DPhil at the University of Oxford (~2000–2004). He served as a fellow and trustee at the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies (~2004) and professor at International Theravāda Buddhist Missionary University (attested 2013).
